novel_features.name: Cert expiry audit
novel_features.description: See every SSL certificate across your whole fleet sorted by days to expiry, before a client site goes insecure.
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining installs, domains, and certificates across every account in local SQLite; the portal shows one install at a time.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when asked about certificate expiry anywhere in the fleet instead of walking installs one API call at a time.

novel_features.name: Backup staleness audit
novel_features.description: Find production installs whose latest completed backup is older than a threshold you set.
novel_features.rationale: Requires the latest-completed-backup-per-install join across the whole fleet, which only exists in the local mirror.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Answers 'which prod installs are unprotected right now' in one call instead of N backup-list calls.

novel_features.name: Version drift audit
novel_features.description: Fleet-wide PHP and WordPress version distribution with outlier filters, plus per-site environment drift detection.
novel_features.rationale: Aggregates versions across all synced installs and compares environments within a site — a cross-account rollup no endpoint provides.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it when asked which installs run outdated PHP/WordPress or whether staging matches production.

novel_features.name: Deploy guard
novel_features.description: Gate a deploy: create a checkpoint backup, wait until it completes, then optionally purge cache, with CI-friendly exit codes.
novel_features.rationale: Compounds the backup lifecycle (requested to in-progress to completed) and cache purge into one scriptable gate no other tool offers over the official API.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it before any deploy that needs a verified restore point; it blocks until the backup actually completes.

novel_features.name: Overage projection
novel_features.description: Project month-end billable visits and storage against account limits and flag accounts trending over.
novel_features.rationale: Fetches live limits and month-to-date usage for every account in one pass and projects forward at the current daily rate — a cross-account overage rollup no single endpoint provides.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it to warn about overages before they land on an invoice, not after.

novel_features.name: Domain health audit
novel_features.description: One list of everything blocked across launches: unverified domains, domains without cert coverage, dangling redirects.
novel_features.rationale: Joins domains, certificates, and redirect targets fleet-wide in local SQLite — the launch checklist the portal scatters across tabs.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it to find every domain still blocking a launch instead of re-checking installs one by one.

novel_features.name: Reverse domain lookup
novel_features.description: Resolve any domain name to the install, site, and account that serve it, plus cert and redirect status.
novel_features.rationale: A single local join across four synced tables; the live API has no domain-to-install reverse index.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it first when a support ticket names a domain and you need to know which install and account own it.

narrative.headline: Every WP Engine Hosting Platform API operation, plus a local fleet mirror that answers cross-account audit questions the portal cannot.
narrative.value_prop: Manage sites, installs, domains, SSL, backups, and cache across every WP Engine account from one terminal. Sync the whole fleet into local SQLite, then run audits no API call can answer: cert expiry ('audit certs'), backup staleness ('audit backups'), PHP version drift ('audit versions'), and domain health ('audit domains'). 'audit usage' projects month-end overages from live plan limits, and 'guard' turns backup-then-deploy-then-purge into one CI-safe command.
narrative.auth_narrative: WP Engine uses HTTP Basic auth with an API User ID and Password generated at my.wpengine.com/api_access (enable API access on your account first). Set WP_ENGINE_API_USERNAME and WP_ENGINE_API_PASSWORD in your environment — the same variables the community SDKs use. Rate limits are undocumented server-side; the client retries 429s with backoff automatically.

quickstart.comment: Verify the CLI is wired up and see which credentials it will look for
Build the local fleet mirror that powers every audit
Resolve a client name to its install without knowing UUIDs
Fleet-wide question the portal cannot answer: who is on old PHP
Preview the deploy gate: backup, wait for completion, purge CDN

troubleshoots.fix: Generate API credentials at my.wpengine.com/api_access and export WP_ENGINE_API_USERNAME and WP_ENGINE_API_PASSWORD; run 'wpengine-pp-cli doctor' to confirm

troubleshoots.symptom: Local-mirror audits (certs, backups, versions, domains) return empty results
troubleshoots.fix: Those audits read the local mirror; run 'wpengine-pp-cli sync --full' first and re-run ('audit usage' is live and needs no sync)

troubleshoots.symptom: 429 Too Many Requests during bulk operations
troubleshoots.fix: WP Engine does not publish rate limits; the client already retries with backoff — space out cron-driven bulk syncs rather than tightening the loop

troubleshoots.symptom: 404 Not Found when passing an install name
troubleshoots.fix: Endpoint commands take UUIDs; resolve names first with 'wpengine-pp-cli search "name" --type installs'

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI for WP Engine hosting platform operations: inventorying accounts, sites, and installs; gating deploys on completed backups; purging caches; managing domains, TXT verification, and SSL certificates; and auditing the fleet for cert expiry, backup staleness, version drift, and usage overages. It shines for agencies managing many installs across multiple accounts, where every portal answer is one-install-at-a-time.
anti_triggers: Managing WordPress content (posts, pages, plugins, themes) — use WP-CLI over SSH or the WordPress REST API; this CLI manages the hosting platform, not WordPress itself
WP Engine Smart Search AI / content MCP features — that is a separate WP Engine product with its own API
Billing invoices, support tickets, or portal-only account settings — not exposed by the Hosting Platform API
Downloading a database dump directly — request a backup and create an archive instead (see the installs backups and installs archives commands)

recipes.title: Monday fleet audit
recipes.command: wpengine-pp-cli sync --full && wpengine-pp-cli audit certs --expiring 30d && wpengine-pp-cli audit backups --stale 7d --env production
recipes.explanation: Refresh the mirror, then surface expiring certs and unprotected production installs in one pass.

recipes.title: Gate a deploy on a verified backup
recipes.explanation: Creates a checkpoint backup, blocks until it reaches completed, then purges the CDN cache — exit code tells CI whether to proceed.

recipes.title: Support-ticket triage by domain
recipes.explanation: One local join resolves a domain to the install, account, environment, and cert status that serve it.

recipes.title: Who is trending over their plan
recipes.explanation: Projects month-end billable visits and bandwidth against plan limits from live month-to-date usage — no sync needed.

recipes.title: Fleet PHP distribution in one query
recipes.explanation: The whole fleet is local SQLite — group any synced resource by any field without an API call.
